# 5. System Architecture Overview

An O-CPS participant is organized as a layered stack. The stack is conceptually identical in vehicles and in RSUs; implementations differ in which layers are populated and which interfaces are exposed to external control.

## 5.1 Stack Diagram

```text
+---------------------------------------------------------------+
|  Application Layer                                            |
|    C-ACC Group Protocol | Slipstream Mode | Intersection Assist|
+---------------------------------------------------------------+
|  Perception & Fusion Layer                                    |
|    Normalized Perception Profile | World Model | Trust Weights|
+---------------------------------------------------------------+
|  Message Layer                                                |
|    PerceptionSummary | Intent | GroupState | Attestation      |
+---------------------------------------------------------------+
|  Security Layer                                               |
|    IEEE 1609.2 / ETSI TS 103 097 | SCMS / C-ITS PKI | MBD     |
+---------------------------------------------------------------+
|  Transport / Network Layer                                    |
|    BTP + GeoNetworking (ITS-G5) | PC5 sidelink transport      |
+---------------------------------------------------------------+
|  PHY / MAC Layer                                              |
|    C-V2X PC5 (LTE-V2X / NR-V2X) | ITS-G5 (802.11p/bd)         |
+---------------------------------------------------------------+
```

## 5.2 Layer Responsibilities

| **Layer** | **Responsibilities** | **Normative References** |
| --- | --- | --- |
| PHY / MAC | Radio transmission and reception; channel access; congestion control. | 3GPP TS 36.213, TS 38.213; IEEE 802.11p/bd |
| Transport / Network | Geocast routing (ITS-G5), sidelink transport (PC5), message segmentation and reassembly. | ETSI EN 302 636 series; 3GPP TS 23.285 |
| Security | Message authentication, pseudonymity, misbehavior detection, revocation. | IEEE 1609.2-2022; ETSI TS 103 097 v2.1.1 |
| Message | O-CPS wire formats and encoding (§9). | This document |
| Perception & Fusion | Normalized perception profile, world-model maintenance, trust-weighted fusion. | This document; ETSI TS 103 324 (informative) |
| Application | Cooperative behaviors that consume the world model and produce advisory or control outputs. | This document |

## 5.3 Interfaces

An O-CPS vehicle implementation exposes the following internal interfaces:

- **V-PERCEPT: **inbound interface from the vehicle’s local perception stack. Consumes object lists and pose estimates in the implementation-specific format of the onboard ADAS.
- **V-CTRL: **outbound advisory interface to the vehicle’s ADAS/control stack. Produces gap targets, lane-keeping biases, and Slipstream state transitions. Never authoritative.
- **V-HMI: **outbound interface to the driver-facing HMI. Surfaces cooperative state and solicits driver authorization where required.
- **V-CRED: **interface to the vehicle’s hardware security module (HSM) for private-key operations and attestation. MUST be protected by secure boot and SecOC.
- **V-DIAG: **diagnostic and logging interface. Emits signed diagnostic records for fleet-owner retrieval; does not expose any externally-transmitted message contents.
